--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Sofia (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you making time. Quick round-robin — we'll do intros then get into network and pilot stuff. Marcus and Ivy and Jared are with me from Redwood.
[00:15] Ravi (Hightide): Hey all, Ravi here, head of platform at Hightide. We've got Laura our CTO, Diego who runs DevOps, and Maya from security. We're excited to get started.
[00:30] Sofia: Great. Goal for today — make sure we have the intake for onboarding, understand whether you'll go Hosted, Dedicated, or Private, and set the pilot success metrics. If anything feels off please interrupt.
[00:45] Ivy (Redwood SE): Quick technical note: we usually ask for a small traffic sample and peak qps distribution plus typical sequence length so we can size batchers and KV cache profiles. Even a CSV with 1k lines helps.
[01:10] Diego (Hightide): Sure, we can extract logs. Right now production traffic averages ~120 rps with burst to ~850 rps for two 20-minute windows per day. Typical prompt length is 300 tokens but some analytics jobs go to 1.2k tokens.
[01:35] Marcus (Redwood CSM): Perfect — Diego, could you drop that by Friday 8/14? That helps Ivy for Dedicated sizing estimate.
[01:45] Diego: Yep, we'll get that to you.
[01:52] Laura (CTO): Our main concerns: latency SLO under 200ms for standard customer-facing flows, data residency for EU customers, and encryption-at-rest using our existing KMS if possible.
[02:10] Maya (Security): Also need audit logs retained for 365 days and SSO via SAML. We'll need to see SOC 2 docs and encryption key control options.
[02:30] Sofia: All noted. For KMS we support customer-managed keys in Private and Dedicated deployments; Hosted can integrate with an external KMS via key wrapping but we need to align on specifics. We'll share the security pack after this call.
[02:50] Ravi: Sounds good. Can you spell out the differences operationally between Dedicated and Private? We're leaning private for regulatory customers but Dedicated might be cheaper but less isolated.
[03:10] Ivy: Sure. Dedicated is reserved capacity within Redwood's control plane but with logical isolation and tenant-level data separation; you get committed throughput and SLA targets. Private means a customer VPC or on-prem footprint with a private control plane and full network isolation. Private offers stronger compliance posture but higher ops coordination.
[03:40] Jared (Onboarding): For Private we work with your network team to establish peering, routing, and firewall rules; we usually run a connectivity checklist and a short preflight test (NAT, MTU, egress rules). We'll send that checklist.
[04:05] Maya: We'll need the checklist early — we have change windows and firewall admins to schedule.
[04:15] Sofia: We'll put the VPC checklist in the runbook. Marcus will share runbook and pilot template by Friday.
[04:24] Diego: On the latency target — 200ms seems tight if we're talking high token counts. How does Redwood achieve that with batching? We don't want batching to inflate tail latency.
[04:40] Ivy: Good callout. Redwood's runtime supports dynamic batching and latency SLO aware routing; you can pin latency-sensitive routes to a small-batch, low-latency pool or use pre-warmed Dedicated nodes for predictable tails. For long context jobs, we recommend asynchronous jobs or a separate worker pool with higher cost-per-token but tolerant latency.
[05:10] Ravi: Ok so maybe split workloads — customer chat under 200ms on Dedicated low-latency pool, analytics jobs run on a cheaper quantized variant.
[05:25] Marcus: That pattern is common. We'll draft a suggested mapping for your routes.
[05:34] Laura: What about observability? We need per-route cost and token-level tracing plus traces tied back to request ids in our Sentry stack.
[05:45] Ivy: Redwood Console exposes per-route token costs, latency histograms, and you can add trace hooks or forward spans to your tracing backend. We have a small tracer shim that sends traces to OTLP collectors; we'll include integration notes.
[06:05] Diego: Good — can you also expose KV cache hit rates? That impacts cost/perf a lot.
[06:12] Ivy: Absolutely, KV cache metrics are surfaced, and we can suggest prefix caching heuristics based on your prompt sets.
[06:25] Laura: On billing — we need a clear picture of delta between Hosted and Dedicated. We might pilot Hosted for speed, but if Dedicated reduces cost under heavy use we want to switch.
[06:40] Marcus: We'll provide a cost comparison model. Ivy will give a sizing estimate for Dedicated and note quantization options.
[06:52] Sofia: Quick logistics — who owns the security review internally? Is that Maya?
[06:58] Maya: Yes, I'll lead it. We'll need SOC 2, data flow diagrams, key handling docs.
[07:08] Sofia: We'll push the security pack to you and set a follow-up for the deeper security session.
[07:15] 
[07:30] (Transcript jump, mid-call technical deep-dive)
[07:30] Ivy: For the Dedicated sizing, given the traffic Diego shared, we should consider two flavors: low-latency pool sized for 200ms SLO for chat routes, and a high-throughput quantized pool for analytics. I'll prepare a cost delta table with GPU types.
[07:50] Diego: What GPU types would you recommend? We run on GCP and have good relationships with NVidia Ampere instances.
[07:58] Ivy: For that topology we usually recommend a mix — A100s for low-latency high-precision instances and T4s/GPU-optimized cheaper nodes for quantized workloads. If you're using a private VPC on GCP we can place Dedicated nodes close to your instances to minimize egress latency.
[08:20] Laura: Are there any blockers for data residency in EU? We need EU-only tenancy for certain clients.
[08:30] Marcus: We can provision Dedicated islands in EU regions or a Private VPC in EU; need to confirm contractual data residency terms. Marcus: I'll flag this in the contract doc.
[08:45] Maya: Also curious about audit log retention and who can access logs — we need role separation.
[08:54] Jared: Audit logs can be exported to your logging bucket or SIEM; we support retention policies and RBAC controls. We can show the settings in the Console.
[09:10] Sofia: Next: pilot scope. Proposal: 4-week pilot, two routes (chat and analytics), success metrics: chat p50 < 120ms, p95 < 200ms, analytics throughput >= current baseline with cost delta reported. Agree?
[09:30] Ravi: That sounds reasonable. Also need uptime target for pilot — 99.5%?
[09:38] Marcus: For pilot we can commit to monitoring and a best-effort SLA; formal SLA will be part of Dedicated contract. 99.5% for pilot is reasonable as a target.
[09:50] Laura: Timeline wise we want pilot starting early September if possible.
[09:56] Marcus: Let's aim to start pilot week of Sept 6. That gives time to complete network intake and security review.
[10:06] 
[10:20] (Security corner of conversation)
[10:20] Maya: A couple specific asks — we need to verify KMS integration options, key rotation policy, and whether Redwood keeps plaintext keys in control plane backups.
[10:35] Ivy: Short answer: for Private we can support customer-managed keys stored in your KMS; Redwood does not hold plaintext keys. For Hosted, there's a key wrapping approach and we can outline the tradeoffs. We'll include a KMS integration doc.
[10:55] Maya: Great. Also need to see past pen-test reports or plan for one.
[11:03] Sofia: We will provide SOC 2 Type II report and coordinate a security questionnaire.
[11:12] 
[11:20] (Wrap and next steps)
[11:20] Sofia: To wrap up — Diego provide traffic sample by 8/14; Marcus will send runbook + VPC checklist by 8/13; Ivy to post Dedicated sizing and cost delta by 8/14; Maya to send compliance list by 8/16. We'll schedule SE deep-dive for Private deployment week of 8/17 and book pilot start for the week of 9/6 pending intake.
[11:45] Ravi: Sounds good. One more question — do you have reference customers in our vertical? We're in travel + bookings and need low-latency search and routing.
[12:00] Marcus: We do have a retail/booking customer reference; Marcus will share a short case study link.
[12:10] Laura: Ok thanks everyone. Appreciate the clear plan.
[12:20] Sofia: Thanks all, we'll follow up with the docs.
[12:30] (Call ends)
